steps.path: Phone → any conversation, and Phone → Files
steps.headline: This is what done means for remote access batches 2 and 3.

rows.statement: The phone's copy of a conversation comes from whichever desktop window holds it, so closing one window never empties the phone.
rows.threshold: a conversation dragged to a second window still reaches the phone, in a dev instance

rows.statement: When the phone has no conversation of its own yet, it opens the one the desktop is showing.
rows.threshold: first connect, and after its conversation is deleted, in a dev instance

rows.statement: After a refresh that came back incomplete, the phone keeps what you were reading instead of clearing it.
Switching the desktop between chat and terminal never switches the phone, whether browser or Android app.
rows.threshold: pass/fail, checked on a browser and on Android

rows.statement: The phone shows a conversation only from the computer's copy, so no message or tool step appears twice after a reconnect.
After sign-in the conversation fills in as soon as the phone says it is ready, not after a fixed wait.
rows.note: though we should optimize/speed this up as much as possible for the best ux.

rows.statement: From the phone, Files shows what the desktop shows, with the same private paths hidden.
The phone previews text up to 1 MB and images and PDFs up to 10 MB; above that it offers Download.
rows.threshold: text to 1 MB, images and PDFs to 10 MB

rows.statement: Every file on the phone has a Download button that saves to the phone's downloads folder without blocking the chat.
rows.threshold: a large download lands in the phone's downloads folder while the chat stays usable

rows.statement: Removing a device from the computer also ends its right to download files.
A file the phone cannot preview shows its name, size and a Download button instead of a refusal.
The phone's file list updates by itself while the assistant changes files on the computer.
rows.threshold: a new file appears on the phone without leaving the screen

rows.statement: While the phone reconnects, a grey line above the messages says so and your draft stays put.
After a refresh that did not finish, an amber line says the conversation may be out of date and offers Refresh.
Pressing Refresh turns the line grey while it catches up, then shows Up to date briefly before the row disappears.
rows.threshold: Up to date shows for 2.5 s

rows.statement: Projects → Files on the phone shows the desktop's folder view: folders, files, search, grid or list.
Tapping a file on the phone opens it in the desktop's viewer, with ‹ Files to go back and Download in the toolbar.
Pressing Download shows a notice that the file is being saved to this device; a refusal says why.
A file over the phone's limit is never fetched; a card shows name, size, kind, the limit and Download.
rows.threshold: 24.0 MB PDF shows the card; previews stop at 1 MB for text and 10 MB for images and PDFs

rows.statement: A phone preview runs in the same sealed box as on the desktop, and a downloaded file is saved, never opened as a page.
A failed file list shows the real error with Retry, and a phone browser never shows the desktop's window buttons.
